items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 HAS bonemeal height gates (unlike 1.21.7): SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget = ServerLevel && isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(getMinimumHeight)); AzaleaBlock = same + 2 and fluid above empty; MushroomBlock = feature exists && AbstractHugeMushroomFeature && HugeMushroomFeatureConfiguration && isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(4+foliageRadius)). The port's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:331-360) matches in form, but tree_minimum_height (growth.rs:437) reads json["trunk_placer"]["base_height"] at the JSON top level while the stored feature JSON (verified in .local/horizon-client/26.2/worldgen/features.json) nests it under config — configured_json (worldgen/live.rs:234) returns the raw whole feature JSON {"type":..., "config": {...}} — so it always returns 0. Vanilla trunk base heights: oak 4, spruce 5, mangrove 2, azalea 4, birch 5, jungle 4, acacia 5, cherry 7 (dark/pale oak have no primary tree, correct by luck). Same nesting bug for mushrooms: the port reads json["foliage_radius"] top-level (bonemeal.rs:343) but it lives under config (brown=3, red absent, default 2); the port always uses 2 — red correct by luck, brown's gate is pos.y+6 instead of pos.y+7. isBonemealSuccess (sapling/azalea 0.45, mushroom/fungus 0.4) matches vanilla exactly. The 1.21.7 over-strict form (refusing a lone dark/pale oak sapling) is GONE — the port comment explicitly says canGrow is 26.3-only. Fix note: read config.trunk_placer.base_height and config.foliage_radius (configured_json's only other caller is the mushroom check).
items.title: Bonemeal validity too permissive at the build ceiling: sapling/azalea/mushroom height gates read the wrong JSON level (MUTATED from 1.21.7)

items.evidence: Vanilla PointedDripstoneBlock.canGrow requires the fluid at pos.above(2) to be WATER and a source (isSource()). The port (speleothem.rs:104-107) checks only fluid.kind() == FluidKind::Water. Flowing water two blocks above the stalactite start lets dripstone grow in the port, not in vanilla. The rest of the speleothem logic matches exactly (growth chance 0.011377778, canGrow via link/blockToGrowOn, max length 2 sulfur / 7 dripstone, 50/50 grow-down vs stalagmite-below, maybeTransferFluid probabilities, falling-stalactite damage max(1+pos.y-fall.y, 6)).
items.title: Dripstone grows under flowing water (missing isSource check in canGrow)

items.evidence: Vanilla ChorusFlowerBlock.randomTick proceeds when above.y <= getMaxY() (320) — bytecode if_icmple 28. The port (tick.rs:1425, chorus_flower_random_tick) returns early when above_pos.y > max_y() - 1, i.e. above.y >= 320. A flower at pos.y == 319: vanilla still ages/branches (horizontal targets at y=319 are in-bounds); the port returns early and the flower stays forever young. The rest of the chorus logic matches exactly (age<5, support/pillar logic, height < 2 || height <= rand(5 or 4), grow-up with allNeighborsEmpty + empty at +2, branch attempts rand(4) + pillar?1:0, events 1033/1034, age-5 death). Note: the analogous vine up-branch guard (pos.y < max_y() - 1 vs vanilla pos.y < maxY) is NOT a defect — at y=319 vanilla's up-branch has no observable effect either (no block can exist at y=320 to attach to).
items.title: Chorus flower never ticks at the build ceiling (off-by-one: > max_y()-1 vs <= maxY)

items.evidence: Vanilla BellBlock.isProperHit (bytecode read in full) requires click_y > 0.8123999834060669 (hit the upper part of the bell) plus a non-Y face plus attachment/axis rules (floor: facing axis == hit axis; single/double wall: axes differ; ceiling: always). The port (redstone.rs:1432, bell_hit) requires click_y <= 0.8124f32 — inverted. Hits at the top ring ring in vanilla but not in the port; hits at the bottom ring ring in the port but not in vanilla. The attachment/axis arms match; bell_ring (block event 1 + sound volume 2.0 pitch 1.0 + BLOCK_CHANGE) matches vanilla attemptToRing (null direction falls back to facing; the port passes facing directly — same result). Bell neighborChanged (powered toggle + ring), placement, survive and updateShape all match.
items.title: Bell isProperHit height comparison inverted (rings on low hits, not high hits)

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 5 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: block ticks, interaction, survival, support, updates, breaking — 1,196 blocks grouped by Java class chain. Worktree: sweep-26.2, branch parity-sweep-26.2, synced to main 732c800f; vanilla ground truth is 26.2's OWN jar/data only. sounds.json/lang files are absent from the prepared data (VM lacks the official launcher's asset index 32.json) — expected, not a defect. A service restart wiped /tmp mid-run, destroying the first set of javap dumps; all findings were preserved in the run record and the dumps needed were re-created afterwards — no finding rests on a lost dump alone.
systemic_note: 1.21.7's two systemic causes both evaporate for 26.2 because 26.2 IS a 26.x version. (1) Class-name drift: gone — the export carries 294 distinct class names, 273 known in level/classes.rs, and the 26 unmapped names are all terminal classes falling back to a mapped ancestor (furnaces, skulls, leaves, weathering copper, glass, AmethystBlock); zero unmapped non-terminal classes; the jar confirms FarmlandBlock, SpreadingSnowyBlock, SnowyBlock, DirtPathBlock, NetherFungusBlock, NetherRootsBlock, SpeleothemBlock, SulfurSpikeBlock, PointedDripstoneBlock, and the absence of FletchingTableBlock/FarmBlock. (2) Absent 26.x tags: gone — every tag the port reads exists in 26.2's block-tags.json (grows_crops, overrides_mushroom_light_requirement, cannot_support_snow_layer/support_override_snow_layer, cannot_support_seagrass, cannot_support_kelp, support_override_cactus_flower, speleothems, maintains_farmland, prevents_nearby_leaf_decay, supports_vegetation, supports_cactus/sugar_cane/bamboo, supports_stem_crops/fruit, supports_crimson_fungus/roots, sniffer_egg_hatch_boost); all 8 #-references in block support fields resolve. What remains is four small logic slips, each a single wrong comparison or a wrong JSON path: a feature-JSON nesting bug (B5-G15), a missing isSource() check (B5-G16), an off-by-one at the build ceiling (B5-G17), an inverted height comparison (B5-G18). The port otherwise matches vanilla 26.2 method-for-method, including where 26.2 differs from both 1.21.7 and 26.3 (waterlogged-sapling tree growth leaves water; canDestroyEgg has no spawn-protection check; tripwire re-check delay 0). Oracle failures have NEW causes vs 1.21.7 (ChunkMap ctor arity, onEquippedItemBroken ItemStack→Item, MaterialBaker abstract method) except B5-O01, which keeps the Prediction cause.
